slides.0.title: Washington I: the Columbia Valley
slides.0.subtitle: The Columbia Valley, Yakima Valley and Red Mountain
slides.1.title: The Columbia Valley: a vast AVA
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Scale
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Approved 13 December 1984; more than 11 million acres (sources range from 11 to 11.52 million)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Share
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Holds about 99% of the state's vineyard acreage (over 59,000 acres)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Soils
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Windblown sand and silt (loess) over gravel and slackwater sediment on basalt; well drained but low in nutrients
slides.1.content: The Columbia Valley is an umbrella AVA that most Washington wine can carry on its label.
slides.2.title: Yakima Valley: the first AVA
slides.2.highlights.0.title: 4 April 1983
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Washington's first AVA and the nation's 28th; about 699,520 acres
slides.2.highlights.1.title: History
slides.2.highlights.1.content: In 1869 Charles Schanno planted the first vines; William Bridgeman's 1914 vineyard supplied cuttings for many later ones; in 1961 a University of Washington group planted Pinot Noir and other vinifera at Sunnyside
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Sub-AVAs
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Includes Red Mountain (2001), Snipes Mountain (2009), Candy Mountain (2020), Goose Gap (2021) and others
slides.2.content: Yakima is one of Washington's earliest regions and contains several smaller sub-AVAs.
slides.3.title: Red Mountain: small, hot and red
slides.3.highlights.0.title: 10 April 2001
slides.3.highlights.0.content: About 4,040 acres, with about 2,382 planted in 2025; Washington's fifth AVA
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Desert climate
slides.3.highlights.1.content: A 187-day growing season and about 3,370 degree days; days average about 90°F in the growing season and nights fall below 50°F
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Varieties and soils
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Mostly red: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Sangiovese, Cabernet Franc, Syrah; very gravelly, alkaline soils with calcium carbonate
slides.3.content: Red Mountain is small, hot and dry, focused on structured reds.
